findings.where: Header nav on the first screen, desktop and phone: 'Profile', 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog'
findings.fault: All three nav items go to the same place, the article specimen (#article). 'Profile' promises Mark's background but drops the visitor on a blog post about PPP law. Three different labels share one destination, so the nav cannot be told apart and leads nowhere its labels say.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer weighing Mark as a consultant clicks 'Profile' to check his experience, lands mid-page on an article, and has to work out that the page has no profile. The founder, judging the first screen, would also find the nav hollow.

findings.where: Article specimen: the numbers of the three-item list (1., 2., 3.)
findings.fault: The list numbers are set in house blue, which this page reserves for links. Its own note beside the article says 'blue only where something can be clicked'. So inside the article blue means two things: a link (the PDF row, the replay control) and a static list number.
findings.who_objects: A reader on the article page learns that blue means clickable, then meets blue numbers that do nothing. Angélique, adding articles, inherits a rule the template already breaks.

findings.where: Article specimen: the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process … PDF ↓'
findings.fault: The row carries a download arrow and 'PDF', so it promises a file. The link only jumps to #article, the top of the same article, and no download happens.
findings.who_objects: A reader who clicks to get Mark's lecture slides is moved up the page with no file and no explanation. The brief names the PDF list as part of 'the product'.

findings.where: Header lockup on the first screen, desktop and phone: the name 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the logo
findings.fault: The name leads the lockup in the place where a site's name is a home link, set off by its own divider. It is static, while only the logo beside it links home. Clicking the most prominent part of the lockup does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on an inner page (an article) clicks Mark's name to get back to the homepage, as on most sites, and nothing happens.

findings.fault: This is a button (it acts here) but wears a link's look: blue, underlined text. The page reserves the underline for links that go somewhere, so the one button on the page reads as navigation.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the motion expects a link to take them elsewhere rather than replay the animation in place. It is minor because the label's verb makes the action clear.
